page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features a 6-core, 12-thread Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 12 dedicated vCPUs alongside 24.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 25 MB of L3 cache, standard AVX support, AES cryptographic instructions, and BMI2, though modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX are absent.

Hardware configurations lack bundled local storage and onboard GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage and standard compute engines. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps. Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates moderate compute capacity, posting a PassMark CPU score of 11,610.14 and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 1,166.0 and 5,654.0 respectively. While cached read bandwidth reaches 620.37 GB/sec, large uncached write operations drop to 24.54 GB/sec, reflecting memory architecture limitations under heavy streaming write scenarios.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance targets CPU-bound tasks rather than memory-heavy applications. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression process at 26.01 GB/sec, and the server sustains 9.94 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.12 GB/sec static web throughput. However, large model handling is constrained, with 7B LLM inference yielding low throughput. This profile suits batch processing, Clang code compilation, web tier serving, and distributed build nodes where elevated clock rates compensate for modest per-core RAM allocation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.3xlarge is a compute-oriented virtual server powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, it delivers 12 dedicated vCPUs derived from 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 24.0 GB, maintaining a strict 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU acceleration, and operates with a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results position the server in the middle performance tiers, achieving 11,610.14 in PassMark CPU tests, 5,654.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 9.94 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Due to its balanced compute frequency and lack of local NVMe storage, this instance is suited for Clang software compilation, web serving, CI/CD worker nodes, and general compute-heavy microservices.
